pr_title: [Python] `read_csv` can now read from a file-like object.
pr_body:
This PR fixes #6442 

Through the `fsspec` support that was recently added by @Mause, we create a MemoryFileSystem that we use to temporarily store objects.
This way when `read_csv` is called with a file-like object instead of a path, we can store it in our filesystem, assign it a random name, and forward that name as if it is a path.
Then when the "path" is fed to the filesystem, it will forward it to our MemoryFileSystem and create a FileHandle that we can read from like normal.
pr_comments:
There is still one problem with this implementation though:
We currently have no way to clean up the temporary files when we're done with them

Though maybe we can override the 'close' method of the filesystem to also delete it - though that would mean some operations that require opening + closing multiple times break when using this..

I have an idea that fixes the "never deleting files from the object filesystem" issue

I'm thinking of overriding the RegisteredObject class to also add a string
You construct it by giving it the filesystem object + the name of the file
In the destructor we delete it from the filesystem - using the filename

issue_context.title: [Python] `read_csv` only accepts a filepath
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

The `read_csv` method in DuckDB is meant to be a replica of `pandas.read_csv`, so it should also accept different types of `filepath_or_buffer`, like it's counter part does

### To Reproduce

```py
import duckdb
from io import StringIO

string = StringIO("c1,c2,c3\na,b,c")
duckdb.read_csv(string, header=True)
```
```
┌─────────┬─────────┬─────────┐
│   c0    │   c1    │   c2    │
│ varchar │ varchar │ varchar │
├─────────┼─────────┼─────────┤
│ a       │ b       │ c       │
└─────────┴─────────┴─────────┘
```

### OS:

MacOS

### DuckDB Version:

master

### DuckDB Client:

Python

### Full Name:

Thijs Bruineman

### Affiliation:

DuckDB Labs

- [X] I agree

### Have you tried the steps to reproduce? Do they include all relevant data and configuration? Does the issue you report still appear there?

- [X] I agree
comments: Might be able to reuse some of the fsspec code for this? As it already does some work to wrap python file objects
I have a message from Mark suggesting something just like this ;)

Likely we will need to register a subsystem with an internal protocol ("duckdb_string_io_" or something similar)
Then add the file with a generated name, forward this file with the attached protocol: "duckdb_string_io_://{random_name}"

Then through the VirtualFileSystem it will be matched by its protocol, and from there the PythonFileSystem will do its job

Actually it's not that straight forward,
I think I have to write a fsspec implementation that contains the StringIO object(s), and forwards the `read` call to the object.

I would have thought there would exist a fsspec filesystem implementation that does this already?

It might be worthwhile to create our own string-backed file system class instead of relying on fsspec, as this might have other use cases in other languages as well. Perhaps it could be used for #6448, for instance.
just speaking to Thijs, StringIO is just an example - we should accept anything that implements IOBase

review_comments: What's the rationale behind adding this method, instead of just using `'name' in list_filesystems()`?
Just wanted a efficient way to check, the existing route returned a py::list - so no real reason, but it also doesn't hurt anyone, right?
For bonus points, make this a `Union[str, IOBase, TextIOBase]` 😉
